citation: Adrion ER, Aucott J, Lemke KW, Weiner JP (2015). Health Care Costs, Utilization and Patterns of Care following Lyme Disease. PLOS ONE 10(2):e0116767.
verification: Uploaded full PDF reviewed, including methods, Tables 2 and 4 and limitations.
population: Commercially insured ages 0–64, continuous enrollment required
cost_metric: Insurer allowed amounts over 12 months; not patient out-of-pocket alone or gross charges
price_year_status: A single inflation-adjusted dollar year was not identified in reviewed text; publication year must not be substituted.

findings.measure: Adjusted excess total medical cost: Lyme group vs matched controls
Adjusted excess cost within Lyme group: >=1 PTLDS-related code vs none

limitations: Symptom-related diagnosis codes are not a validated PTLDS diagnosis or demonstrated functional decline
No medical-record confirmation of each Lyme case
Excludes uninsured people, Medicare-age adults and many people with interrupted coverage
Only 12-month costs; no lifetime economic burden or work-loss valuation
Two adjusted differences use different comparison groups; do not add them or combine with Hook societal totals
Historical associations do not establish app savings or causal treatment-delay effects
